QF.id: AIFM CIII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_2

question.text: Aravalli Long-Short Fund has 40 investors holding units with aggregate value of investment of INR 800 crore. At a meeting called under Regulation 29, investors representing INR 612 crore (by value of investment) vote in favour of winding up. Does the resolution pass?

answer.text: Yes — INR 612 cr / INR 800 cr = 76.5%, above the 75% threshold
No — headcount of voters is not disclosed; headcount majority is also required
No — winding-up resolutions need unanimous 100% consent
Yes, but only if SEBI concurrently directs winding up

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 29 requires 75% of investors BY VALUE OF INVESTMENT to pass the winding-up resolution. 612 / 800 = 76.5%, which clears the 75% threshold. Headcount is NOT a secondary requirement — the AIF Regulations are purely value-weighted. A SEBI direction to wind up is a SEPARATE independent trigger, not a conjunction. The Trap: Unanimity (option C) is wrong — AIFs never need 100% for winding up. Dual headcount + value (option B) borrows from mutual-fund unit-holder rules. SEBI concurrence (option D) confuses the independent SEBI-directed trigger with a joint requirement. Note: The workbook fixes the 75%-by-value-of-investment Regulation 29 threshold; operational guidance on running the test off a specific NAV register is not part of the syllabus.
